Overview

Component building can become a complex process. The ODS Guidelines facilitate the building of new components, compliant with the plugin, expanding on all the required steps to achieve this.

Guidelines section overview

Component Structure
Component Properties
Component Variants
Component Styles
Colours & Schemes
Naming Convention
RADD Specific Rules
The contents in the guide are categorised in thematic sections, and subsections.
There are 3 distinct tags marking each subsection:

savings  Mandatory rule
Always follow the rules tagged with “Mandatory rule” to make your component plugin compliant and avoid code issues.

standardOnBackground  Checked by plugin
Rules with this tag will be checked by the plugin. The plugin will expose errors and/or warnings the designer needs to address, and offers a quick and easy way to locate them in Figma.
Please note: not all mandatory rules are checked by the plugin. Always make sure to follow the guidelines and check manually if needed.

warning  Best practice
The “Best practice” tag indicates, what standards ODS components are following. Considering the best practices enhances the quality of design and code and facilitates collaboration.

End to end process

In addition to the Create product-specific Components guideline, the phases you might go through when building a component are:

1
Research
What are the product requirements? - Check OneDS component gallery. - What do other mature design systems do? Check Material Design System, check Carbon Design System, etc.
2
Outline Functionalities
Check if this can be done by an existing ODS component - Check if this is a special case, if so, should it be a global ODS component or a product specific one? Global ODS components it should be handled by the ODS team. - What does the component do?
3
Build the component
If you are part of the ODS team, build the component in the Figma OneID Exploration File. - If you are part of a Product team, build the component in your team’s library file. - Go to Create product-specific Components guideline.
Start from the most complex variant, addressing every single element in the component. - Build all other necessary variants by hiding/exposing layers in the left layer panel.
4
Stress test it*
Try applying lots of text. - Try resizing the component horizontally. - Try resizing the component vertically. - Try 200% font increase. How does it look? - Try 400% font increase. Does it still work? Does it get cropped out of view? If so, you might need to revise your component. - Try Multi-Select a layer. Does it appear in all variants? If not, something is probably out of place. - Ask for feedback from your accessibility expert.
5
Plugin check*
Run the RADD Plugin in Design mode. - Make sure you toggle between the correct Library Check (Mobile / Web). - Correct any mistakes that might have slipped through.
6
Prototype the component*
Switch into Prototype mode in Figma and prototype your Component. - Address the Component States (Standard, Hovered, Pressed and Focused). - Address Selected/Checked use cases, if there are any.
7
Start documentation
Start documenting your Component following the ODS Guidelines. The more you get done, the better it is. - Address use cases, behaviours and property table. This will be helpful for the Developer. - Check Colour Schemes: does your Component work in every colour scheme or is it restricted in a specific case?
8
Dev review*
Move your Component to the Production file. - Tag a developer from the Plugin Team to review your component. - Tag a Developer from the Web Team and from the Mobile Team to review your component and also via Jira Ticket.
9
Check developed component
Compare your Figma Component to the Developed Component on Storybook and Sample App.
10
Signoff!
Congratulations! You're done!
*Rework might be necessary in steps that are marked with an asterisk
